title: 菜“不正宗”，真的是罪过吗
title_en: Is "Not Authentic" Really the Worst Thing a Dish Can Be?
summary_zh: 一篇议论文：作者认为，拿“正不正宗”给餐厅定罪往往站不住脚——同一道菜家家做法不同，漂洋过海更要变；真正该问的是诚不诚实、用不用心。文中也承认了“正宗派”的合理之处。
body: Read enough restaurant reviews and you will notice that one accusation stings more than any complaint about slow service or cold soup: the food, someone declares, is not authentic. It is a strange charge, when you think about it, because it assumes that every dish has a single correct version, fixed somewhere in the past and waiting to be betrayed. Anyone who has eaten the same dish in two neighbouring towns knows how quickly that assumption falls apart under scrutiny. The variance between households alone is enormous; ask three grandmothers for the proper way to fold a dumpling and you will get four answers and at least one argument. When food travels overseas, it changes further, and not because cooks are careless. Ingredients differ, customers bring different habits, and a small family restaurant has to stay commercially viable on a street full of competitors. The noodle shop that adds a little sugar, or serves its lunch special with an ice-cold soda because that is what local office workers order, is not committing a crime; it is doing what cooks have always done. None of this means that authenticity is meaningless, and I will make one concession to the purists: when a restaurant markets itself as a faithful taste of a particular region and then serves something unrecognisable, diners have every right to feel misled. Notice, though, that the problem there is honesty, not tradition. Indeed, the look of authenticity is now easy to manufacture, with handwritten menus, mismatched bowls and a black-and-white photo of an unnamed village, and it often fools the very critics who are most obsessed with it. What troubles me most is the tone of morality that creeps into these debates, as though eating an adapted dish were a small betrayal and enjoying it a character flaw. That tone strikes me as inappropriate for something as generous as cooking. A better question for any reviewer is simpler: was the food made with care, and would you go back? If the answer to both is yes, the label on the menu hardly matters.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the writer's position?
options: Judging food mainly by authenticity misses what matters more, such as honesty and care
Restaurants abroad should follow traditional recipes exactly
Online reviewers are usually right to criticise adapted dishes
Authenticity matters only in expensive restaurants
questions.evidence: was the food made with care, and would you go back?

questions.prompt: What does the writer admit to the "purists"?
options: That adapted dishes usually taste worse than the originals
That diners may fairly feel misled when a restaurant's claims are false
That handwritten menus are a reliable sign of tradition
That cooks abroad are often careless with ingredients
questions.evidence: diners have every right to feel misled

questions.prompt: What point does the writer make about handwritten menus and mismatched bowls?
options: The look of authenticity can easily be faked
Such details make a restaurant more expensive
Critics prefer restaurants with modern design
Traditional restaurants always serve better food
questions.evidence: the look of authenticity is now easy to manufacture

questions.prompt: What does "commercially viable" mean in "stay commercially viable"?
options: able to make enough money to keep going
popular with tourists
approved by food critics
run by a single family
questions.evidence: stay commercially viable on a street full of competitors

vocabulary.example: As a concession to the children, we stopped for ice cream on the way home.

vocabulary.meaning: （商业上）能维持下去的；可行的
vocabulary.example: Without more customers, the little bookshop is no longer viable.
Some reality shows manufacture drama by cutting conversations in half.

vocabulary.meaning: 纯粹主义者；讲究正统的人
vocabulary.example: Coffee purists say you should never add sugar.
I felt misled when the "sea view" turned out to be a car park.

expressions.note: 插入语，引出一个容易被忽视的角度，语气轻松
fall apart 散架；under scrutiny 在仔细审视之下，合起来指论点一细看就站不住
强调对方的反应是合理的：You have every right to be angry.
the very + 名词 表示“正是、恰恰”，常带讽刺或强调
比 I think 更委婉、书面：That strikes me as unfair.
hardly 本身就是否定，不要再加 not

knowledge.quote: as though eating an adapted dish were a small betrayal
knowledge.explanation: as though 后用 were，表示与现在事实相反的假设（吃改良菜当然不是背叛），带作者的讽刺；正式文体里即使主语是单数也用 were。

knowledge.quote: a single correct version, fixed somewhere in the past and waiting to be betrayed
knowledge.explanation: 过去分词 fixed（被固定的）和现在分词短语 waiting to be betrayed 并列作后置定语，一被动一主动，画出人们想象中的“标准答案”。

knowledge.quote: What troubles me most is the tone of morality that creeps into these debates
knowledge.explanation: What 引导的名词性从句作主语，相当于 The thing that troubles me most；把真正的重点留到句末，是议论文常用的强调句式。

speaking: 你吃过“不正宗”但很好吃的菜吗？用 1 分钟说说你觉得“正宗”重不重要，举一个例子，并回应一个反对意见。
writing: 写一篇 220–260 词的议论文 Does authenticity matter in food?：要有明确论点、一个让步（I will make one concession...）和反驳，并用上一个 What... is... 主语从句。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 the problem there is A, not B 指出一场争论真正的问题所在。
task.model: the problem there is honesty, not tradition

title: 把绘本里的“龙”译成英文
title_en: What Do You Do with a Kind Dragon? A Translator on Picture Books
summary_zh: 一位童书译者谈翻译中文绘本的经历：中国的龙温和智慧，英语小读者却会想到喷火怪兽；结尾的说教要不要软化？读完你会明白“忠实”在翻译里到底指什么。
body: Q: Your latest project is a picture book about a dragon who looks after a mountain village, so what made it difficult to translate? Mira: The dragon, almost entirely. In the original, he embodies everything a farming village might hope for: rain at the right time, patience and a kind of unhurried wisdom. But the moment an English-speaking child sees the word "dragon", they picture smoke, a pile of gold and a knight arriving to fight it. Q: Did you consider changing the word? Mira: For about a week, yes, and I tried "sky serpent", "river spirit" and even leaving the Chinese name untranslated. Every option either sounded like a video game or forced the reader to stop and decode it, which is fatal in a book meant to be read aloud at bedtime. In the end I kept "dragon" and let the pictures do the work, because once children see him gently carrying a lost goat home, they revise their expectations remarkably quickly. Q: How faithful should a translator be? Mira: Faithful to the experience rather than to every word, so a child reading the English should feel what a child reading the Chinese feels, even if that means I have to intervene. Q: Does that extend to the morality of the story? Mira: Up to a point, yes. The original manuscript ended with a line that spelled out the lesson rather sternly. In Chinese it sounds natural, almost like a proverb, but in English it felt like a teacher wagging a finger, which some parents would find inappropriate at bedtime, so I softened it and let the dragon's compassion speak for itself. Q: Isn't there a danger that softening it will conceal something about the original? Mira: It's a fair worry, which is why the English text was subsequently checked line by line by the author herself, and she rejected two of my changes. She was right both times, but I'd still argue that early literacy depends on children loving how a story sounds, and a book that reads like homework ends up unread on the shelf.

questions.prompt: Why was the word "dragon" the hardest part of the translation?
options: English has no word for a creature like this
English-speaking children tend to imagine a dangerous monster
The author asked Mira not to use the word
The illustrations showed a different animal
questions.evidence: they picture smoke, a pile of gold and a knight arriving to fight it

questions.prompt: What does Mira mean by being faithful "to the experience rather than to every word"?
options: English readers should feel what Chinese readers feel
Every word should be translated exactly, whatever the effect
Children should choose which words they prefer
Cultural notes should be added at the end of the book
questions.evidence: a child reading the English should feel what a child reading the Chinese feels

questions.prompt: What is the interview mainly about?
options: How a translator adapts a picture book so that it feels right in another language
Why children should read stories in the original language
How to write a picture book from scratch
Why dragons are dangerous in Chinese stories
questions.evidence: Faithful to the experience rather than to every word

questions.prompt: What does "intervene" mean in "even if that means I have to intervene"?
options: read the text aloud
ask for more money
step in and make changes
give up the project
questions.evidence: even if that means I have to intervene

vocabulary.example: To my grandmother, the old kitchen embodies the whole family's history.
It took me a minute to decode my friend's handwriting.
The teacher had to intervene when the argument got too loud.
"Sit down," the coach said sternly, and everyone sat.

vocabulary.meaning: 读写能力（early literacy 指幼儿早期阅读能力）
vocabulary.example: Reading aloud every night is good for a child's early literacy.

expressions.text: let the pictures do the work
expressions.note: let sth do the work 让某样东西自己发挥作用，不必多解释
亲子阅读常用：books meant to be read aloud
spell out 把意思一条条说清楚，有时暗示“太直白”
比喻居高临下地说教；wag a finger at sb
let sth speak for itself 不需要额外解释，事实本身就有说服力
check / read sth line by line 表示非常仔细地看

knowledge.quote: a child reading the English should feel what a child reading the Chinese feels
knowledge.explanation: what 引导宾语从句作 feel 的宾语，相当于 the thing that...；前后两个对称的 a child reading... 把两种读者放在一起对比。

knowledge.quote: they picture smoke, a pile of gold and a knight arriving to fight it
knowledge.explanation: 现在分词短语 arriving to fight it 作后置定语修饰 a knight，表示正在进行的主动动作，比 a knight who arrives... 更有画面感。

knowledge.quote: forced the reader to stop and decode it, which is fatal in a book meant to be read aloud at bedtime
knowledge.explanation: which 引导非限制性定语从句，指代前面整件事（读者被迫停下来猜词），而不是某一个名词。

speaking: 选一个在中英文里联想很不一样的词（比如“龙”“狗”“红色”），用 1 分钟解释差别，并说说如果你是译者会怎么处理。
writing: 写 200–240 词，回答 Should a translator change a story to suit new readers?：举一个例子，给出你的立场和一个让步，用上 rather than 和一个 what 引导的名词性从句。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 Faithful to A rather than to B 说说你做某件事时真正看重的是什么。
task.model: Faithful to the experience rather than to every word

title: 现场解说为什么这样说话
title_en: Why Live Commentary Sounds the Way It Does
summary_zh: 一篇讲解文：广播解说和电视解说分工有何不同，两位解说员的风格为何要有差异，解说又有哪些陷阱。读完你会听懂体育解说背后的“行规”。
body: Anyone who has tried to describe a football match to a friend over the phone knows how hard it is to keep talking while things keep happening. Live commentary is a craft built around precisely that problem, and its habits make more sense once you see the pressures behind them. Radio commentators carry the heavier load, because their listeners can see nothing at all; they must establish who has the ball, where it is and what might happen next, often in a single breath. Television commentators, by contrast, are encouraged to say less, since the pictures already carry most of the information, and the skill lies in adding what the camera cannot show: a player's limp, a coach's frustration, the reason a team has suddenly stopped attacking. Most broadcasts divide the work between two voices. The first describes the action, while the second, usually a former player, offers analysis, and the variance in their styles is deliberate, giving listeners both rhythm and depth. During a pause, the analyst might provide a breakdown of how a goal was scored, replaying each pass step by step. Commentary has its traps, too. Excitement can tip into exaggeration, and bias tends to creep in quietly, especially when a broadcaster is covering a home team. When a commentator says something unfortunate on air, such as a careless joke or a wrong name, producers may intervene through an earpiece, but the words have already gone out. Many broadcasters now offer interactive options, letting viewers choose a different audio track or switch the commentary off altogether, and some coaches say it is beneficial to rewatch matches in silence, judging the play without another voice in their ears. Yet most viewers keep the commentary on, and the reason is revealing: good commentary does not merely report events but decides which moments are worthy of remembering, turning a blur of movement into a story with a beginning, a middle and an end.

questions.prompt: According to the explainer, what is the main job of a television commentator?
options: To describe every movement on the screen in detail
To add information that the pictures cannot show
To keep talking so that there is never any silence
To make the match sound more exciting than it is
questions.evidence: the skill lies in adding what the camera cannot show

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence suggest about why most viewers keep the commentary on?
options: It gives them more accurate information than the pictures
It is difficult to switch off on most channels
It hides the mistakes that players make
It helps turn a match into a story they can remember
questions.evidence: decides which moments are worthy of remembering

questions.prompt: What is the explainer mainly about?
options: How former players become coaches
How live commentary works and why it sounds the way it does
The history of a famous football club
Why radio is better than television
questions.evidence: Live commentary is a craft built around precisely that problem

questions.prompt: What does "creep in" mean in "bias tends to creep in quietly"?
options: disappear completely
be removed by producers
be announced loudly
appear gradually without being noticed
questions.evidence: bias tends to creep in quietly

vocabulary.example: Before we argue, let's establish what actually happened.
The slow start of the film is deliberate, not a mistake.
The coach gave us a breakdown of every mistake we made in the first half.
Saying the queue went round the block was a slight exaggeration.
Fans often accuse the referee of bias towards the home team.

expressions.note: 形容说得又快又密：She told me the whole story in a single breath.
对比两类事物的连接语，书面、口语都常用
sth lies in + 名词/动名词：The secret lies in the timing.
常指某种状态过了头：Confidence can tip into arrogance.
explain / replay sth step by step
广播电视用语：say something on air / be on air

knowledge.quote: the variance in their styles is deliberate
knowledge.explanation: 主语的中心词是 variance（单数），in their styles 只是修饰语，所以谓语用 is 而不是 are。

knowledge.quote: the analyst might provide a breakdown of how a goal was scored, replaying each pass step by step
knowledge.explanation: 现在分词短语 replaying each pass step by step 作伴随状语，说明分析员“边回放边讲解”，逻辑主语是 the analyst。

knowledge.quote: Radio commentators carry the heavier load, because their listeners can see nothing at all
knowledge.explanation: because 引导原因状语从句，解释广播解说为什么更难；because 通常用来给出对方未必知道的新原因。

speaking: 你喜欢开着解说看比赛、直播或游戏视频吗？用 1 分钟说说好解说和差解说的区别，并举一个例子。
writing: 写 200–240 词的讲解文，介绍你熟悉的一种“现场解说”（体育、游戏直播、导游讲解等）：它的规矩、难点和常见问题，用上 by contrast 和一个分词作状语的句子。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 good X does not merely..., but... 说出你心目中好老师、好朋友或好书的标准。
task.model: good commentary does not merely report events but decides which moments are worthy of remembering

title: 爷爷的汽水厂重聚日
title_en: A Letter from Grandpa's Old Soda Factory
summary_zh: Mei 给远在海外、没能赶回来的 Jun 写信，讲她怎样张罗了一场汽水厂老员工的重聚，又从一位老人口中听到了爷爷不为人知的一面。读完你会学到私人长邮件里自然的叙事和抒情方式。
body: Dear Jun, I know you were sorry to miss the reunion at Grandpa's old soda factory, so here is the long version I promised, written on the train home. You'll laugh, but I somehow ended up as the chief organizer, which mostly meant fighting a quiet war with local bureaucracy for permission to open the doors for a single afternoon. When we finally got inside, the place looked like a museum of junk: stacks of wooden crates, a calendar stopped at some long-forgotten June, and that enormous bottling machine whose breakdowns have been a family joke for as long as either of us can remember. It's strange to think that Grandpa and a handful of neighbours used to manufacture, right there, an orange drink that nobody outside the region had ever heard of. Former workers started arriving after lunch, some with walking sticks and others with grandchildren, and every one of them seemed to have saved up a story for the day. One woman told me that during the worst breakdown, when the machine stood silent for most of a summer, Grandpa kept paying everyone out of his own savings and managed to conceal it from Grandma until the bank called. We always thought of him as stern, didn't we? Hearing about that quiet compassion has rearranged something in my memory of him. By the time I stood up to give the short tribute, my stomach was in knots and I'd abandoned my notes entirely. So I simply said that he used to call the factory his destiny, half as a joke, and that I'd never understood why until I saw the people in that room. I wish you had been there, honestly. Since you're overseas until the spring, I'm posting you the one thing I brought home: an unopened bottle that a man in a flat cap slipped into my bag, the orange faded to the colour of weak tea. Love, Mei

questions.prompt: How did the reunion change Mei's view of her grandfather?
options: She realised he had been careless with the family's money
She found out that he had hated running the factory
She learned that he had secretly wanted to move overseas
She discovered a kindness in him that she had not known about
questions.evidence: Hearing about that quiet compassion has rearranged something in my memory of him.

questions.prompt: What was the hardest part of being the organizer, according to Mei?
options: Persuading former workers to come
Getting official permission to open the building
Repairing the old bottling machine
Writing the speech for the tribute
questions.evidence: fighting a quiet war with local bureaucracy for permission to open the doors for a single afternoon

questions.prompt: What does the description of the bottle, "faded to the colour of weak tea", suggest?
options: It was a new product from the factory
It had been kept unopened for a very long time
It had been made in another country
It had been opened and refilled
questions.evidence: the orange faded to the colour of weak tea

questions.prompt: What does "conceal" mean in "managed to conceal it from Grandma"?
options: hide
explain
repay
announce
questions.evidence: managed to conceal it from Grandma until the bank called

vocabulary.example: Our class reunion is next month, and I'm already nervous.
Our old car has had so many breakdowns that we've given it a name.
He couldn't conceal how pleased he was with the result.
My piano teacher looked stern, but she was actually very kind.
We abandoned the picnic when it started to pour.

expressions.note: end up as + 身份/角色：I somehow ended up as the team leader.

expressions.text: for as long as either of us can remember
expressions.meaning: 从我们俩记事起就一直
expressions.note: for as long as I can remember 表示“一直以来、从我记事起”

expressions.meaning: 自掏腰包（用自己的积蓄）
expressions.note: pay for sth out of one's own pocket / savings
形容非常紧张焦虑，也可以说 My stomach is in knots.
say sth half as a joke 说得半真半假

expressions.text: I wish you had been there
expressions.note: I wish + 过去完成时，表达对过去的遗憾，私人信件里很常见

knowledge.quote: I wish you had been there, honestly.
knowledge.explanation: I wish 后接过去完成时 had been，表示对过去的遗憾（事实上对方没来）。如果是对现在的愿望，则用一般过去时：I wish you were here.

knowledge.quote: that enormous bottling machine whose breakdowns have been a family joke for as long as either of us can remember
knowledge.explanation: whose 引导定语从句，表示所属关系（机器的故障）；先行词是物时同样可以用 whose。

knowledge.quote: Hearing about that quiet compassion has rearranged something in my memory of him.
knowledge.explanation: 动名词短语 Hearing about that quiet compassion 作主语，谓语用单数 has；整句含蓄地说出“我对爷爷的印象变了”。

speaking: 用 1 分钟讲一位长辈让你意外的一面：你原来怎么看他/她，后来听说或看到了什么，现在的看法有什么变化。
writing: 给一位没能参加某次家庭聚会或活动的亲友写一封 200–240 词的邮件，讲讲现场发生的事和你的感受，用上 I wish you had been there 和一个 whose 定语从句。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 It's strange to think that... used to... 写一个让你感慨的地方或人。
task.model: It's strange to think that Grandpa and a handful of neighbours used to manufacture, right there, an orange drink that nobody outside the region had ever heard of.
